## `slot`

Run builds on one shared pool of build slots.

`slot <command…>` sends the command to the slot daemon, which queues it until enough slots are free, runs it, streams its output back and exits with its code. Every build that goes through the daemon shares one GNU-make jobserver, so cargo, rustc and make draw parallelism from the same pool and the machine is never oversubscribed.

```text
slot [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

- `--local`: Run the command here, without the daemon (default `false`)
- `--here`: Keep the job in this host's pool, never on a build node: for a step that needs this host's credentials while it runs (a clone, a fetch, a push). `slot status` shows `local: here: needs this host` under it (default `false`)
- `--tokens`: Slots the job holds, in place of the count slot derives from the command. For work the daemon cannot see, such as a script that starts `docker run --cpus 4`: `slot --tokens 4 ./build.sh`. The daemon caps it at the slots in circulation (the pool less the headroom), so the job never waits forever. Ignored with `--local` (env `SLOT_TOKENS`)
- `--priority`: The job's queue level: queued `urgent` jobs get free slots first, then `high`, `normal` and `low` ones; with no slot free, an `urgent` job starts on one the headroom holds back. A rule set with `slot priority set` for the job's repository wins over it. Ignored with `--local` (env `SLOT_PRIORITY`)
- `--timeout`: How long the job may run, counted from its start, in place of the daemon's run-time limit (`slot run-limit`): seconds, or a number with `s`, `m` or `h`, such as `90s`, `30m` or `1h`. The daemon ends a job that runs longer (SIGTERM, SIGKILL 5 s later) and the job exits 124. It is capped at the most a job may name, 1 h unless `slot run-limit --max` changed it. A `timeout` command in front of the job's command does not extend it. Ignored with `--local` (env `SLOT_TIMEOUT`)
- `--fetch`: With `SLOT_HOST` set: after the job exits 0, copy PATH back from the build server into the checkout. PATH is relative to the repository root; `target/…` is read from the job's target directory on the server. Repeat for more paths. Without `SLOT_HOST` the output is already here and this does nothing

### `slot serve`

Run the daemon: the slot pool, the job queue and the web UI

```text
slot serve [OPTIONS]
```

- `--socket`: Unix socket clients connect to (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)
- `--http`: Web UI address; `off` disables it (default `127.0.0.1:7411`)
- `--tokens`: Build slots in the pool (jobserver tokens); default: the number of CPUs
- `--go-tokens`: Slots a go job holds; go's -p is set to match (default `4`)
- `--test-threads`: Threads a test runner in a job may use when the caller sets none: `RUST_TEST_THREADS`, `NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS` and `GOMAXPROCS` (go jobs get their slot count). Default: a quarter of the pool, at least 2. Local jobs only: a job synced from another host gets its width, the free CPUs at its start split over the jobs that started in the last 5 s, and a lower count its caller set is raised to it
- `--cpu-quota`: Whether a headroom also sets systemd `CPUQuota` on the daemon unit, a hard cap on every job together; `false` keeps only the token limit (default `true`)
- `--state-dir`: Jobserver FIFO and job log
- `--ws-root`: Where remote clients sync workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/ws`)
- `--cache-root`: Target dirs and caches for synced workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/cache`)
- `--memory-max`: systemd `MemoryMax` per job, for example 24G
- `--keep-jobs`: Finished jobs kept in memory and shown in the UI (default `500`)
- `--cpu-weight`: systemd `CPUWeight` for every job (interactive apps default to 100); 0 leaves it unset. Applied to the daemon's own unit at start (default `20`)
- `--call-headroom`: Call mode: headroom while a call uses the microphone or the camera, percent; 0 turns call mode off. `slot headroom --call` changes it at run time and that value is kept (default `40`)
- `--call-off-after`: Seconds without capture after which a call counts as ended and the headroom goes back (default `120`)
- `--call-ignore`: Applications whose capture is not a call (level meters, mixers), comma-separated; replaces the default list (default `claude,pavucontrol,pwvucontrol,easyeffects,helvum,qpwgraph,coppwr,noisetorch`)
- `--sccache-watch`: Watch this user's sccache servers and write back the jobserver tokens a server lost, once it had none free for 60 s while compiles waited, and append each server's counters to `cache.jsonl` in the state directory once a minute; `false` turns both off (default `true`)
- `--min-free-disk`: A job waits while the filesystem of its directory or of `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` has less free space than this, GB; 0 turns it off. Above `--evict-below`, eviction starts here instead (default `25`)
- `--min-free-disk-light`: The disk floor of a job whose last 5 runs of the same command in the same repository used no compile server and built into no target directory, GB; at most `--min-free-disk`, and no job starts below it. A first run waits at `--min-free-disk`. 0 lets such a job start on any free space. Default: the value of `--min-free-disk`
- `--min-free-memory`: A job waits while available memory, less what jobs that started in the last 30 s still take, is below its expected peak (from earlier runs) plus this, GB; 0 turns it off. A job alone in the pool runs anyway (default `4`)
- `--upgrade-hold`: After `systemctl --user reload slot`, the longest time no new job starts while jobs still run, seconds. Then jobs start again, and the next hold begins when the running jobs are expected to end within it (from earlier runs of the same command) or none runs. 0 never holds (default `60`)
- `--promote-after`: A queued `normal` or `low` job that has waited longer than this is ordered as `high`, so no level waits forever; 0 never promotes. `slot priority promote-after` changes it at run time; a value set that way wins over this option until `slot priority promote-after default` removes it (default `1800`)
- `--pass-for`: A queued job may be passed by later jobs of its own level only until it has waited this long: by a job predicted to run 5 s or less, and by a job that fits in the slots a larger request collected and cannot use yet. From then on it starts before every job that came after it. A job of a lower level never passes it. 0: nobody passes; the queue is served by level, then arrival (default `300`)
- `--cache-budget`: For remote clients: GB the target directories of synced workspaces may take together. Before a remote job starts, the least recently used target directories and their source copies are deleted while the total is over this, or while the disk has less than `--min-free-disk` free; a workspace with a queued or running job is kept. 0: no budget, only the disk floor evicts (default `0`)
- `--seed-copy`: For remote clients: how the first job of a new worktree copies the target directory of another worktree of the same repository. `reflink`: only a reflink copy, none where the filesystem has no reflinks (a byte copy of a large target directory can take longer than the build it saves). `copy`: a reflink where the filesystem has them, else a byte copy. Never hard links (default `reflink`)
- `--evict-below`: When the filesystem of a local Cargo target directory has less free space than this, GB, delete target directories that jobs built into, least recently built first, until it has 10 GB more. The mark is `--min-free-disk` when that is larger, so eviction runs whenever jobs wait for disk; a job that starts to wait makes it look at once. A directory a queued or running job builds into or whose checkout it runs in, one built in the last 2 h, and one a process uses are kept. 0 turns it off, whatever `--min-free-disk` is. `slot evict-below` replaces this mark at run time (default `40`)
- `--evict-dry-run`: Only report in the journal and `slot status` which target directories eviction would delete. `dry_run` in `<state-dir>/evict.json`, read every minute, wins over this (default `false`)
- `--handover`: On `systemctl --user reload slot`, re-execute at once and hand the running and queued jobs, their slots and their clients to the new binary; `false`, or a new binary older than 0.11.0, uses the `--upgrade-hold` rule instead (default `true`)
- `--sandbox`: Run every job in a sandbox (bubblewrap): the whole filesystem read-only and in its own pid namespace; writable are only the job's checkout, its target directory, a private /tmp and the download caches of cargo and Go. Other workspaces, other jobs' target directories and the user's runtime directory are hidden. Without a working `bwrap` the daemon does not start (default `false`)
- `--cluster-file`: The host configuration file: its `[remote.<name>]` tables are the remote nodes the daemon polls every 5 s and shows in `GET /api/nodes` and the web UI. `off` reads none (env `SLOT_CLUSTER_FILE`)
- `--sandbox-write`: One more path a sandboxed job may write, for example a package manager's store; repeat for more
- `--sandbox-fixed-paths`: With --sandbox: mount each job's checkout at /work/src and its target directory at /work/target, so every worktree of a repository builds at the same paths. The job then runs without a rustc wrapper: the compile cache server outside the sandbox cannot read sources at those paths (default `false`)
- `--same-path-root`: A directory under which a remote client may mirror its tree at the tree's own absolute path (`SLOT_REMOTE_SAME_PATH=1` on the client), so absolute paths into the tree work on this server. Repeat for more; `SLOT_SAME_PATH_ROOTS` lists them separated by `:`. Give `slot shell` the same list (env `SLOT_SAME_PATH_ROOTS`)

### `slot proxy`

Bridge stdin/stdout to the daemon's socket (remote clients run this over ssh)

```text
slot proxy [OPTIONS]
```

- `--socket`: The daemon's socket (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)

### `slot shell`

ssh forced command for a build server: runs only the sync, sibling, fetch, proxy and cancel steps named in `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`

```text
slot shell [OPTIONS]
```

- `--socket`: The daemon's socket, for `slot proxy` (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)
- `--state-dir`: The daemon's state directory
- `--ws-root`: Where remote clients sync workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/ws`)
- `--cache-root`: Target dirs of synced workspaces (default: `<state-dir>/cache`)
- `--http`: The daemon's web address, for the `state` step (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)
- `--same-path-root`: A directory under which a client may sync its tree to the tree's own absolute path and fetch from it, as with `slot serve`; repeat for more (env `SLOT_SAME_PATH_ROOTS`)

### `slot gate`

Serve gate directories: builds in a sandbox that can open FIFOs there, but cannot reach the daemon's socket, queue in the pool and run in their sandbox. The client sets `SLOT_GATE=<dir>`

```text
slot gate [OPTIONS] --dir <DIR>
```

- `--dir`: A directory the sandbox sees at the same path, on the filesystem of the daemon's state directory (the pool FIFO is hard-linked into it). Repeat for more sandboxes; `SLOT_GATE_DIRS` lists them separated by `:` (env `SLOT_GATE_DIRS`)
- `--socket`: The daemon's socket (env `SLOT_SOCKET`)
- `--state-dir`: The daemon's state directory, which holds the pool FIFO

### `slot run`

Run a build command; use this when the command's name is also a slot subcommand

```text
slot run [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>...
```

- `--tokens`: Slots the job holds, as `slot --tokens N`; capped at the slots in circulation. Ignored with `--local`
- `--priority`: The job's queue level, as `slot --priority LEVEL`
- `--timeout`: How long the job may run, as `slot --timeout DURATION`
- `<COMMAND>`: The command and its arguments

### `slot status`

Show the pool and every queued and running job

```text
slot status [OPTIONS]
```

- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot headroom`

Show or set the headroom: the share of the CPU kept free for you

```text
slot headroom [OPTIONS] [PERCENT]
```

- `<PERCENT>`: New headroom, percent, 0 to 50; without it, prints the current one
- `--call`: Headroom during a call, percent, 0 to 50; 0 turns call mode off
- `--base`: What the headroom is a share of: `pool` caps the pool at a fixed quota; `machine` lowers the pool's quota by the CPU used outside the pool, so the whole machine keeps the headroom free
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot priority`

Show or change the priority rules: the queue level of every job of a repository

```text
slot priority [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `slot priority set`

Give every job of the repositories PATTERN matches the level LEVEL

```text
slot priority set [OPTIONS] <PATTERN> <LEVEL>
```

- `<PATTERN>`: Repository name or glob, such as `repo-a` or `web-*`
- `<LEVEL>`: `urgent`, `high`, `normal` or `low`
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

#### `slot priority unset`

Remove the rule for PATTERN

```text
slot priority unset [OPTIONS] <PATTERN>
```

- `<PATTERN>`: The pattern of the rule, as `slot priority list` shows it
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

#### `slot priority list`

List the rules

```text
slot priority list [OPTIONS]
```

- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

#### `slot priority promote-after`

Set how long a queued `normal` or `low` job waits before it is ordered as `high`, while the daemon runs

```text
slot priority promote-after [OPTIONS] <SECONDS>
```

- `<SECONDS>`: Seconds; 0 never promotes a job; `default` goes back to the daemon's `--promote-after`. The value applies to the jobs already queued, is kept in `priority.json` in the state directory and wins over `--promote-after` across reloads and restarts, until `default` removes it
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot run-limit`

Show or set the run-time limit: how long a job may run before the daemon ends it

```text
slot run-limit [OPTIONS] [DURATION|off]
```

- `<LIMIT>`: How long a job may run, counted from its start: seconds, or a number with `s`, `m` or `h` (`90s`, `10m`, `1h`); `off` for no limit. The daemon ends a job that runs longer (SIGTERM to its processes, SIGKILL 5 s later) and the job exits 124. The limit applies to the jobs that start after the change, is kept in `limits.json` in the state directory and holds across reloads and restarts
- `--max`: The most a job may name with `slot --timeout`; 1 h until it is set
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot job-parallel`

Show or set the limit on build processes per job: with it a job's compilers run on a bound of the job's own, not on slots of the pool

```text
slot job-parallel [OPTIONS] [N|off]
```

- `<LIMIT>`: Build processes one job may run at once, from 1; `off` for no limit, the default. With a limit N the daemon starts a job without the pool's jobserver and with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` and `MAKEFLAGS=-j` set to N, or to the slots the job holds if that is more (`slot --tokens`): `cargo` and `make` in the job then bound themselves and take no slots of the pool, so the pool limits how many jobs run, not how many compilers. It applies to the jobs that start after the change, is kept in `limits.json` in the state directory and holds across reloads and restarts
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot evict-below`

Show or set the eviction mark: the free space below which the daemon deletes idle Cargo target directories, without a restart

```text
slot evict-below [OPTIONS] [GB|default]
```

- `<MARK>`: Free space, GB, below which eviction deletes idle target directories, from 0 (eviction off) to 100000; `default` forgets the mark and the idle keep, and `serve --evict-below` and 2 h apply again. It replaces `--evict-below` and is raised to `--min-free-disk` when that is larger; the disk hold itself does not change. Eviction looks at once. The mark is kept in `limits.json` in the state directory and holds across reloads and restarts
- `--idle`: The idle keep: eviction keeps a target directory built more recently than this, from 5m to 168h (7 days); 2h until it is set. Kept in `limits.json` like the mark; applies at the next look
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot cpu-limit`

Show or set the CPU limit: the start of a queued job is held while the pool's jobs and the compile cache use more CPUs than a mark

```text
slot cpu-limit [OPTIONS] [CPUs|off]
```

- `<MARK>`: Busy CPUs from which the start of a queued job is held, from 1 (`17`, `17.5`); `off` for no limit, the default. The figure is the CPU time over the last 10 s of the pool's jobs (with the compilers a compile cache server runs for them) and of the rest of the compile cache server, with what jobs that started in the last 30 s are expected to add; work outside both is shown, not counted. Without arguments it prints both parts and the CPUs outside them. A job held for 10 minutes starts whatever the figure says. A mark above the host's CPU count never holds for CPU time (`--pressure` still does). The mark reaches queued jobs within 2 seconds, is kept in `limits.json` in the state directory and holds across reloads and restarts
- `--floor`: Jobs that may always run, whatever the host's CPUs do, from 1; 4 until one is named. `off` forgets it
- `--pressure`: CPU pressure of the host (`some avg10` of `/proc/pressure/cpu`, percent, over 0 and at most 100) from which the start of a queued job is held as well, while the floor's jobs run; `off` forgets it, the default. On a saturated host the CPU time of the pool stops rising at its share while the pressure keeps rising. It needs a CPU mark, holds also with a mark above the host's CPU count, keeps the bound of 10 minutes, and is kept in `limits.json`. Without arguments `slot cpu-limit` prints it and the pressure now
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot admission`

Show or set how queued jobs are admitted: by slots of the pool, or by a share of the CPUs while that share is free

```text
slot admission [OPTIONS] [shares|slots]
```

- `<MODE>`: `slots`, the default: a job holds slots of the pool while it runs, and the pool's size bounds how many run. `shares`: a job asks for a share of the CPUs, predicted from earlier runs of the same command (`--tokens N` asks for N), holds no slot of its own and starts while that share is free in a budget that follows how much slower than their best the jobs run, never above the pool's CPU quota. The pool's slots then bound the build processes inside the jobs, as many as the budget has CPUs. Kept in `limits.json` in the state directory; holds across reloads and restarts
- `--floor`: By share: jobs that run whatever the share says, from 1; 4 until one is named
- `--max`: By share: the most jobs that run at once, at least the floor; 48 until one is named
- `--pressure`: By share: CPU pressure of the host (`some avg10` of `/proc/pressure/cpu`, percent) over which only jobs predicted to run 5 s or less start; 60 until one is named
- `--min-budget`: By share: the least CPUs the budget falls to, at least 1; half the host's CPUs until one is named, and never under the shares of the floor's running jobs
- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

### `slot cancel`

Cancel a queued or running job you submitted; a running job's processes get SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5 s

```text
slot cancel [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

- `<ID>`: Job id, as `slot status` shows it (`#12` or `12`)

### `slot warm`

After a merge to `main`: build the tests of a checkout of `main` at the lowest level, so the next worktree of the repository starts from a built target directory.

Run it in the checkout after it took the merge, for example from its `post-merge` hook. It returns at once; the daemon runs `cargo test --no-run`, or the `warm` command of the checkout's `.slot.toml` (`warm = false` switches it off). The daemon starts one only for a repository a job built on it in the last 24 hours, one at a time per repository, and cancels it when a job of a session waits for slots.

```text
slot warm [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

- `<DIR>`: The checkout of `main` to build; the working directory without it

### `slot sessions`

List agent sessions that build outside the pool, with their commands

```text
slot sessions [OPTIONS]
```

- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)
- `--window`: Seconds of history to average (default `60`)
- `--min-cores`: Leave out sessions below this many cores outside slot, unless a command of theirs runs now; builds outside any agent session are left out below it in any case (default `0.5`)
- `--json`: Print JSON instead of text (default `false`)

### `slot usage`

Show how the pool was shared: slot time, CPU time and queue wait per project, repository or session, from the job log

```text
slot usage [OPTIONS]
```

- `--http`: The daemon's web address (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)
- `--since`: Window ending now: a number followed by m, h or d (default `24h`)
- `--by`: Group by project (the namespace of the repository's remote), repo or session (default `project`)
- `--top`: Rows to print (default `15`)
- `--json`: Print JSON instead of text (default `false`)

### `slot cache`

The compile cache: what the sccache servers did, from the counters the daemon records once a minute

```text
slot cache [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `slot cache refused`

The compiler calls the sccache servers refused to cache, per repository and reason, with hits and misses, and what a repository can do about each reason.

Reads `cache.jsonl` and `jobs.jsonl` in the state directory. A minute's calls belong to the jobs that ran in it with compile-server CPU: to one repository exactly when all of them are its, else split by each job's compile-server CPU rate times its time in the minute (shared). Minutes no such job explains are counted apart.

```text
slot cache refused [OPTIONS]
```

- `--state-dir`: The daemon's state directory
- `--since`: Window ending now: a number followed by m, h or d (default `24h`)
- `--by`: Group by repo or project (the namespace of the repository's remote) (default `repo`)
- `--json`: Print JSON instead of text (default `false`)

### `slot node`

The build nodes of this host: the `[remote.<name>]` entries of the host configuration file, and which node a repository's jobs go to.

Any other `slot node …` command line (`slot node --test`, `slot node build.js`) is a build command that runs Node.js, as before.

```text
slot node [OPTIONS]
       slot node <COMMAND>
```

#### `slot node list`

List the registered nodes: name, state as the daemon sees it (when it answers), whether it takes queued local jobs (spill), whether it is the default node, and the repositories routed to it

```text
slot node list [OPTIONS]
```

- `--cluster-file`: The host configuration file (env `SLOT_CLUSTER_FILE`)
- `--http`: The daemon's web address, for each node's state (env `SLOT_HTTP`, default `127.0.0.1:7411`)

#### `slot node route`

Print the node a job in DIR goes to, as shell assignments of `SLOT_HOST`, `SLOT_SSH`, `SLOT_REMOTE` and `SLOT_NODE_END` (the node's deadline, Unix seconds; left out without one) and an `export` line, for `eval "$(slot node route)"`.

The node is the entry whose `repositories` lists the repository of DIR (the name `slot status` shows), else `default_node`. Reads only the file: no daemon and no network. Exits 3 with one line naming the file when no entry matches or the matched name has no entry.

```text
slot node route [OPTIONS] [DIR]
```

- `<DIR>`: A directory of the checkout; the working directory when absent
- `--cluster-file`: The host configuration file (env `SLOT_CLUSTER_FILE`)

#### `slot node add`

Register a node: write its `[remote.<name>]` entry. A repository listed under another node moves to this one. The rest of the file stays as it was; a file that does not parse is refused

```text
slot node add [OPTIONS] --ssh <SSH> <NAME>
```

- `<NAME>`: Node name: lower-case letters, digits and `-`
- `--ssh`: The ssh command line that reaches the node, host last (`ssh -o BatchMode=yes build-1`)
- `--slot-path`: Path of `slot` on the node; `slot` when absent
- `--deadline`: End of the node's lease, RFC 3339
- `--price-per-hour-cents`: Price per hour, cents
- `--spill`: `false`: the daemon never hands a queued local job to the node
- `--repository`: A repository whose jobs go to the node; repeat for more
- `--default`: Make the node `default_node`: the node of every repository no entry lists (default `false`)
- `--cluster-file`: The host configuration file (env `SLOT_CLUSTER_FILE`)

#### `slot node remove`

Deregister a node: take its entry out. Its repositories then go to `default_node`; removing the default node clears `default_node`

```text
slot node remove [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

- `<NAME>`: Node name
- `--cluster-file`: The host configuration file (env `SLOT_CLUSTER_FILE`)

### `slot hook`

Agent hooks: refuse a build command that would run outside the pool

```text
slot hook [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `slot hook claude-pre-tool-use`

Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook for the Bash tool: reads the event on stdin and exits 2 with the `slot` command to run when the command builds or tests outside the pool. `SLOT_HOOK=warn` adds the advice as context instead of refusing; `SLOT_HOOK=off` allows everything

```text
slot hook claude-pre-tool-use [OPTIONS]
```
